faqs.question: What is the cheapest Halloween costume that still looks like a costume?
faqs.answer: A one-item signal costume: glow sticks taped into a stick figure over dark clothes, or plastic spider rings and stretch web pinned into your hair, at an EST $3 to $7. Pick something people recognise in a small phone photo, because that is where most costumes get seen.

faqs.question: Can I put together a Halloween costume for under $20?
faqs.answer: Yes. A thrifted base garment plus one prop and some makeup covers a prom zombie, a mad scientist or an overworked office vampire at an EST $9 to $18. Keep $3 to $5 back for the extras people forget, such as fang putty or makeup remover.

faqs.question: How much does the average person spend on Halloween?

faqs.question: What is $20 in pounds and rupees for a costume budget?

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to thrift a Halloween costume or buy a new one?
faqs.answer: Thrift usually wins for base garments, at an EST $5 to $20 against $20 to $60 for a new bagged costume. A 2025 US study found second-hand buyers also bought more new clothing (r = 0.58), so the saving only counts if the thrifted piece replaces a new one.

faqs.question: When should I start shopping for a cheap costume?
faqs.answer: Hit the thrift racks in the first two weeks of October, before the good stock goes. The NRF found 49% of US shoppers begin Halloween shopping in September or earlier, and Halloween falls on Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027.

faqs.question: Are light-up costumes safe for small children?

faqs.question: What happens to cheap Halloween costumes after one wear?
faqs.answer: Most are thrown away. US EPA data show only 13% of clothing and footwear was recycled in 2018, so resell a costume in good condition, donate the base garment, or keep it for next year.

faqs.question: Where can I find cheap kids' Halloween costumes?
faqs.answer: Resale apps, school swap rails and neighbourhood groups in early October carry used branded costumes at an EST $15 to $30. Check seams, zips and mask elastic before paying, since children's costumes take hard wear.

faqs.question: Is there a way to show my costume to someone who couldn't be there?
faqs.answer: Yes. Our regular Halloween card holds up to six photos and takes about five minutes, while the premium page holds up to 12 photos plus a voice recording of up to a minute. Both are made for one recipient, not a group.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Cheap Halloween Costumes Built to a $10, $20 or $35 Budget

Cheap Halloween costumes work when the money goes on what people recognise first, the head, the face or the outline, and none goes on fabric detail nobody notices. Under $10 buys one strong signal item, $20 adds a second-hand base garment, and $35 buys a full character with makeup and a light. The reason is where costumes get seen: 48.3% of our 57,456 logged page views were on phones, and a page we host is opened 11.1 times on average, so yours will mostly be judged as a small photo, more than once.

US shoppers plan to put $4.4 billion into costumes in 2026, according to the National Retail Federation. Below are nine costumes priced by tier (EST, with £ and ₹ equivalents), a sourcing comparison and the hidden costs: makeup, batteries and one-wear waste.

## How do you judge whether a costume is cheap?

A cheap costume is one with a low cost per wear once every extra is counted, not one with a low tag. A $12 outfit worn once costs more per outing than a $25 one worn at three parties and a school event.

The [NRF's poll of 7,889 US consumers, fielded 1–9 September 2026](https://nrf.com/media-center/press-releases/nrf-halloween-survey-shows-consumer-spending-expected-to-reach-13-5-billion), found an average planned Halloween budget of $115.14 per person across candy, decorations and costumes. 34% said they would look for items they can reuse or repurpose, and discount stores (39%) were the top place to buy.

Every amount here is our estimate (EST), not a shop's quote, so check shelf prices before you go. Conversions use the ECB reference rates of 13 October 2026, $1 = £0.755 = ₹95.28, and they are not a local price guide: ₹953 goes further in an Indian market than $10 does in a US mall.

## Cheap Halloween costumes by budget: under $10, $20 and $35

Every costume gets four fields in a fixed order: what to buy, where to find it, the EST total and the cost that is easy to forget. The tiers are $10 (about £7.55 / ₹953), $20 (about £15.10 / ₹1,906) and $35 (about £26.40 / ₹3,335), all EST at the 13 October 2026 rate.

### 1. Under $10: glow-stick stick figure

- **Buy:** 15 to 20 bendable glow sticks and clear tape, worn over dark clothes you own.
- **Where:** dollar or pound stores; supermarket party aisles.
- **EST total:** $4 to $7.
- **Hidden cost:** glow sticks last one night and then go in the bin, so this is single-use by design.

### 2. Under $10: lost tourist from 1987

- **Buy:** one loud second-hand shirt, a bum bag, a fold-out paper map and sunscreen smeared on the nose.
- **Where:** a charity shop or thrift rack; the map from a tourist office or your own drawer.
- **EST total:** $6 to $9.
- **Hidden cost:** almost none, because the shirt joins your summer wardrobe. Pick the most patterned one on the rail; at phone-photo size, pattern does the work.

### 3. Under $10: spider-nest hair

- **Buy:** a bag of plastic spider rings and a packet of stretchy web, pinned into hair or a beanie over all-black clothes.
- **Where:** dollar stores from late September.
- **EST total:** $3 to $6.
- **Hidden cost:** the stretch web is a synthetic fibre that sheds, cannot go in household recycling and tangles easily outdoors.

### 4. Under $20: thrifted prom zombie

- **Buy:** a second-hand formal dress or suit, a grey and green eyeshadow palette and cocoa powder for mud.
- **Where:** charity shops, which stock formalwear year round; resale apps for exact sizes.
- **EST total:** $12 to $18.
- **Hidden cost:** the palette. Use cosmetics made for skin, never craft paint, and tear the hem rather than the bodice so the garment can be donated again in November.

### 5. Under $20: mad scientist

- **Buy:** a used lab coat or white chef's jacket, clear safety glasses and hair gel for upright hair.
- **Where:** resale apps and uniform thrift bins; hardware stores for the glasses.
- **EST total:** $10 to $16.
- **Hidden cost:** gel and wash-out hair spray, an EST $3 to $5 more.

### 6. Under $20: overworked office vampire

- **Buy:** a thrifted dark blazer or long cardigan, plastic fangs and red lipstick for the mouth corners. 4.2 million American adults intended to go as a vampire in 2026, per the NRF, so the work-tired twist helps you stand apart.
- **Where:** the thrift rack for the blazer; a dollar store for the fangs.
- **EST total:** $9 to $15.
- **Hidden cost:** cheap fangs often need fixing putty to stay in, about $3 extra.

### 7. Under $35: used licensed character

- **Buy:** a second-hand branded costume, such as the Spider-Man suit 4.6 million US children planned to wear in 2026, per the NRF.
- **Where:** resale apps, school swap rails and neighbourhood groups in early October.
- **EST total:** $15 to $30.
- **Hidden cost:** washing and repairs, so check seams, zips and mask elastic before paying.

### 8. Under $35: the proper witch

- **Buy:** a thrifted black dress or robe, a stiff wide-brim hat and a green or grey face-makeup kit. Witch topped the NRF's 2026 adult list at 4.8 million people, and the hat is what stops yours looking like a black dress.
- **Where:** thrift for the dress; a costume shop for the hat, the one item worth paying full price for.
- **EST total:** $22 to $34.
- **Hidden cost:** makeup remover, about $4 to $6.

### 9. Under $35: ghost miner with a headlamp

- **Buy:** a thrifted flannel shirt, a cheap headlamp and grey face powder for a dusty look.
- **Where:** thrift for the shirt; a hardware store for the headlamp.
- **EST total:** $18 to $30.
- **Hidden cost:** AAA batteries plus a spare set.

## Thrift, dollar store or resale: where cheap costumes come from

The table compares four routes on EST spend for one complete costume and the main catch.

| Source | EST spend for one costume | Best for | The catch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Thrift or charity shop | $5 to $20 | Base garments: dresses, blazers, flannel | Racks thin out by mid-October |
| Dollar or pound store | $3 to $10 | Props, fangs, glow sticks, hair pieces | Single-use plastic, one size only |
| Resale apps | $10 to $30 | Licensed kids' costumes, exact sizes | Postage adds $4 to $8 EST; 3 to 7 days |
| New, bagged costume | $20 to $60 | A complete look in one bag | Thin polyester, usually worn once |

Halloween lands on Saturday in 2026 and Sunday in 2027 (both 31 October), and good second-hand stock is gone by mid-month. NRF data show 49% of shoppers begin in September or before.

Second-hand is not automatically greener, though. In a 2025 nationally representative sample of 1,009 Americans, [buying second-hand clothing went with buying more new clothing, not less](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12504660) (r = 0.58), researchers found, so a thrifted costume only helps if it replaces a new one.

## The hidden costs: makeup, batteries and one-wear waste

The tag is rarely the full price. Three extras can turn a $10 costume into a $20 one, and two of them carry costs not measured in money.

**Makeup.** Face products, remover and setting spray add an EST $6 to $15. Buy skin-safe cosmetics, test a small skin patch seven days before, and stop using anything that stings.

**Batteries.** Light-up costumes and novelty badges often run on button cells. Research published in 2026 in the Journal of Laryngology & Otology puts [US accidental button-battery swallowing at about 6,000 cases a year](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13121042), and 65% of its 561 respondents had never considered the danger, so tape every battery cover shut on a child's costume.

**One-wear waste.** Many bagged costumes are polyester, so read the label. EPA data for 2018 show [only 13% of clothing and footwear was recycled](https://www.epa.gov/facts-and-figures-about-materials-waste-and-recycling/textiles-material-specific-data); landfills took in 11.3 million tons of textiles that year.

Where landfill is not the end point, fire often is. A 2026 analysis estimates [10 to 20 million tonnes of textile waste are burned in the open each year](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13053536) across 137 countries, with South Asia carrying 37% of the emissions.

## After the party: one costume photo, one greeting page

If one particular person missed it, a partner, a best friend or a sibling at university, build them a page instead. Neither Halloween template here works for a party; each one addresses one reader.

[Our regular Halloween card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) suits a quick send: roughly 5 minutes to make, room for six photos, and a haunted-house walk-through where your friend knocks, carves a jack-o'-lantern and clears misted portraits to reveal the costume. The finale is a Boo License naming a costume you assigned them.

[The premium cinematic Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) suits a bigger reveal: about 10 minutes of setup, 12 photo slots for the full before-and-after, an optional unlock time, a voice recording no longer than one minute and a single reply they can send back. Some 38.5% of our creators add a password before sharing, a sensible move for the cocoa-powder close-up.

Planning a costume date rather than sending a greeting? [The Invitation date page](https://subhsandesh.in/date-invitation) asks the question properly, and their yes starts a countdown.

## When spending less on a costume backfires

Spend more on a costume worn ten times a year, for cosplay, drama club or a child who plays dress-up weekly. By the third outing, its cost per wear drops below any $10 option.

Spend more on safety for kids trick-or-treating at dusk, too: a flimsy dark costume with a mask that blocks side vision is a false saving. Add a $3 EST reflective band or a light before any prop.

Our pages have limits as well. Menus are English-only, every page goes to a single person, and neither template sells, rents or designs costumes; when your friend is standing right there in matching face paint, a photo together beats any link.

## Sources

- National Retail Federation, [NRF Halloween survey shows consumer spending expected to reach $13.5 billion](https://nrf.com/media-center/press-releases/nrf-halloween-survey-shows-consumer-spending-expected-to-reach-13-5-billion), 22 September 2026.
- US Environmental Protection Agency, [Textiles: material-specific data](https://www.epa.gov/facts-and-figures-about-materials-waste-and-recycling/textiles-material-specific-data), 2018 data, page last updated 19 March 2026.
- Mizrachi and Sharon, [Secondhand fashion consumers exhibit fast fashion behaviors despite sustainability narratives](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12504660), *Scientific Reports*, 7 October 2025.
- Bayramova et al., [Environmental impact of open burning of polyester and cotton textile waste](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13053536), *Environmental Science and Pollution Research*, 8 March 2026.
- Mahesh, Keogh and Majeed, [Button battery ingestion in children is potentially fatal](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13121042), *Journal of Laryngology & Otology*, 1 February 2026.
